CPU threads for the generation stage (llama.cpp n_threads). Defaults to a value based on device core count (never exceeding it). Too few threads underutilize compute; more than the core count causes contention and slowdowns. Adjust to taste.

CPU threads for the read-source (prefill/batch) stage (llama.cpp n_threads_batch). Defaults to all device cores. Independent of generation threads and adjustable separately; must not exceed the core count.
Randomness temperature. Controls creativity and diversity. For translation, 0.1 (strict literal, highly stable) to 0.7 (better for paraphrase, more natural) is recommended.
Nucleus sampling threshold: only candidates whose cumulative probability reaches 60% are considered. A lower top_p (e.g. 0.6) filters low-probability words for more rigorous translations.
Top-k: each generation draws only from the top 20 most probable candidates, preventing off-topic or wrong-word translations.
Repetition penalty. Mildly penalizes already-generated tokens. 1.05 avoids endless repetition without breaking legitimate repeats (layout, punctuation).
Maximum output tokens per single request. Caps the output length of one translation; not the model context (-c).

Custom Image Translation API Function Description

⚠️ Note: This is an advanced feature that requires you to have basic API call knowledge.

1. Basic Description
This feature allows you to configure your own image translation API, supporting both GET and POST request methods. (For image translation, the POST Content-Type can be either application/json; charset=utf-8 or multipart/form-data. Simply select the appropriate Content-Type in the dropdown menu, and there’s no need to explicitly add it to the request headers below.) All API responses must be in JSON format.

2. Usage Scenarios
Typically, major translation API providers implement their own signature algorithms, making it impossible to integrate via simple GET/POST requests. As such, the practical use case for the custom image translation API is to connect with a translation API interface that you’ve built yourself.

3. Parameter Description
1、Request Method: Can be either GET or POST.
2、Content-Type (POST only): Can be application/json or multipart/form-data.
3、Base URL: Can specify http or https. If no scheme is specified, the default is https.
4、Query Parameters (GET only): Parameters appended to the base URL.
5、Request Headers: Headers sent with the request.
6、Request Body (POST only): Content included with the request.
7、JSON Response Path: Path to retrieve the translation result from the API response JSON.

Note:
1、In "Query Parameters" and the request body with Content-Type set to application/json, use "useimgbase64" to represent the image file to be translated.
2、In the request body with Content-Type set to multipart/form-data, use "useimgfile" to represent the image file to be translated.
3、Additionally, ensure that both "source language" and "target language" codes are included in the "Query Parameters" or "Request Body."

4. Request Examples
GET Request
Base URL:
https://api.example.com/translate

Query Parameters:
Key: img, Value: useimgbase64
Key: source, Value: ja
Key: target, Value: zh

Request Headers:
Authorization = my_custom_token

POST Request
Content-Type:
application/json

Base URL:
https://api.example.com/translate

Request Headers:
Authorization = my_custom_token

Request Body:
Key: img, Value: useimgbase64
Key: source, Value: ja
Key: target, Value: zh

POST Request
Content-Type:
multipart/form-data

Base URL:
https://api.example.com/translate

Request Headers:
Authorization = my_custom_token

Request Body:
Key: img, Value: useimgfile
Key: source, Value: ja
Key: target, Value: zh

5. JSON Response Path
Example 1:
Suppose the successful JSON response is as follows:

{
 "code": 0,
 "msg": "success",
 "data": {
 "translation": "Hello World"
 }
}

Then the JSON response path should be: "data.translation".

Example 2:
Suppose the successful JSON response is as follows:

{
 "code": 0,
 "msg": "success",
 "result": "Hello World"
}

Then the JSON response path should be: "result".(Excludes ".")

6. Before Using This Feature
You can first test the API response using tools like Postman or Reqable. Once the tests are successful, you can enter the relevant parameters into this feature.

Why is my HarmonyOS version 3.0 or greater, but it still says that the Android version is too low?

This is due to the fact that after Huawei updated HarmonyOS (note that it is not HarmonyOS NEXT), its underlying Android API can no longer be visually visible to users. For most newer Huawei phones, HarmonyOS 2.0 supports Android 10 (API 29). HarmonyOS 3.0 is compatible with Android 12 (API 31). However, for some older Huawei models, although HarmonyOS 3.0 has been updated, the underlying Android API has not been updated, and the underlying Android version of some models is still Android 10. As a result, the system still does not meet the requirements of Android 11 (API 30) for this software. Here are some of the known models:\n\nEquipped with Kirin 980 and below models, such as mate20, P30, Nova 5, etc., HarmonyOS 3.0 corresponds to Android version 10 (API 29). The HarmonyOS 3.0 of these models is not really 3.0, and there are many missing features, but the main upgrades are: updating the version number, using the new theme of 3.0, and adding some small features that do not depend on Android 12.
Why do I have granted accessibility permissions, but the software still prompts that I have not obtained accessibility permissions?

This is due to accessibility permissions being reclaimed by the system; Accessibility is a very important permission in Android. Most Android-based systems will revoke accessibility privileges when you exit the software or shut down and restart it, also for security reasons (of course, this software is open source and does not collect any information from you).\n\nKnowing the reason, it is also very easy to solve. As long as the software homepage clicks on the \"? > find the step to grant accessibility permissions - > click \"Go to grant this permission\" - > find the software, then turn off the accessibility permissions of the software, and re-grant them.
Adjust this option in the \"Translation Mode\" and \"API Configuration\" of the Settings page
Why did I click on the hoverball, but there was no translation result for a long time, and finally an error was reported?

This is most likely due to poor internet connections. Many waifu games need to use accelerators, but after using accelerators, it is relatively slow to access the domestic translation API. As a result, the translation will time out and errors will occur.\n\nAt this time, please turn off your wifi, turn on the data data, and then speed up with the accelerator again. At this point, you should be able to use the translation fluently. There is no need to worry about data consumption, generally speaking, when you use the translation mode of \"local OCR recognition + text translation\", the amount of traffic spent is minimal.
Why can\'t I download models, update the software, or see update announcements in the model management page?

This is because downloading models (GitHub/HuggingFace), checking for updates, and fetching announcements all require access to overseas services that are blocked in mainland China. Please enable or switch your VPN and try again. A stable proxy is recommended to ensure smooth network access.
I\'m getting a \"DataInspectionFailed\" or \"Output data may contain inappropriate content\" error during translation?

This is caused by the content safety review mechanism of the API platform. Translation platforms (such as Volc Engine, Tongyi Qianwen, etc.) may block sensitive content, and different platforms have different review thresholds.\n\nSolution: Try switching to a different translation platform or model. For example, switch from Volc Engine to DeepSeek or Tongyi Qianwen.
Manga translation results are missing, inaccurate, or slow?

You can try the following optimizations:

1. Frame the area that needs translation: Precisely selecting the text area improves OCR accuracy and avoids recognizing irrelevant content.

2. Reduce UI interference: Avoid selecting blank areas, game UI buttons, and other non-text content. Reducing unnecessary recognition improves speed.

3. Choose the right translation model: Models with mini, lit, or flash labels have faster response times.

In manga translation debug mode, adjust PP-OCRv5/v6 engine parameters via sliders/switches. Changes take effect immediately. Use ⚙ to toggle the parameter panel, 📊 to toggle debug info.

Parameters below are shared between v5 and v6 (separate storage, may have different defaults). v6-only parameters are listed at the end.

[Shared Parameters (PP-OCRv5 & PP-OCRv6)]

box_thresh — Detection Box Confidence
Det.box_thresh. Default 0.3 (v5) / 0.5 (v6), range 0.01 ~ 0.7. Threshold for keeping detected boxes.
- Text missed → lower
- Noise boxes → raise

unclip_ratio — Box Expansion Ratio
Det.unclip_ratio. Default 1.6. Range 1.0 ~ 3.0 (v5) / 1.6 ~ 2.0 (v6).
Controls detection box expansion (Vatti clipping). Larger values → boxes become larger.
- Characters truncated → increase
- Boxes too large → decrease

text_score — Recognition Confidence
Global.text_score. Default 0.5, range 0.1 ~ 0.9. Filters low-confidence recognition results.
- Translation missing → lower
- Garbled text → raise

limit_side_len — Image Side Length Limit
Det.limit_side_len. Default 1200, range 64 ~ 2048 (pixels). Limits image side length. Used with limit_type.

limit_type — Side Length Limit Strategy
Det.limit_type. Default max, options min / max.
max = scale down long side (preserves speed, recommended for game/manga crops). min = scale up short side (preserves detail, can be slow on thin crops).

large_box_enabled — Large Box Filter
Default Off. Filters detection boxes that occupy too much of the image.
- Large false-positive boxes → enable

large_box_ratio — Large Box Discard Ratio
Default 60%, range 30% ~ 80%. Effective only when large box filter is enabled.

merge_gap — Line Merge Distance Gate
Default 1.5, range 0.5 ~ 5.0. Line merge distance threshold (× font size). Lines beyond this distance are not merged into the same bubble.

[PP-OCRv6 Only]

thresh — Text/Background Segmentation Threshold
Det.thresh. Default 0.3, range 0.1 ~ 0.5. Binarization threshold. Larger values → text regions become smaller.
- Text missed → lower
- Noise boxes → raise

max_candidates — Maximum Candidate Boxes
Det.max_candidates. Default 1000, range 50 ~ 2000. Maximum candidates retained during connected-component analysis.

use_dilation — Morphological Dilation
Det.use_dilation. Default On (true). Applies 3×3 cross-kernel dilation to merge adjacent text regions. Recommended for dense vertical manga text.

min_height — Minimum Image Height
Global.min_height. Default 30, range 10 ~ 200 (pixels). Images below this height skip detection and go straight to recognition.

rec_batch_num — Recognition Batch Size
Rec.rec_batch_num. Default 6, range 1 ~ 12. Number of text lines per ONNX inference batch.
What is the purpose of downloading dedicated OCR recognition models?

PP-OCRv5's Chinese recognition model (rec_zh) is a Chinese-Japanese-English general model that can recognize Chinese, Japanese, and English. When no dedicated model is downloaded, English recognition uses this general model by default.

After downloading a dedicated model, the system automatically switches for better results:

• English model (rec_en): Optimized for English, higher accuracy especially for uppercase/lowercase, numbers, and punctuation.
• Korean model (rec_ko): Dedicated to Korean. Without it, Korean text cannot be recognized.
• Russian model (rec_ru): Dedicated to Russian/Cyrillic script. Without it, Russian text cannot be recognized.

How to download: Go to Settings → Model Management → PP-OCRv5 Recognition Models, tap download. Models are small (7~13MB) and take effect immediately without restarting.

How to verify: When translating manga in a non-default language (e.g. English), a toast “using dedicated recognition model: rec_en” appears, confirming the dedicated model is active. If no toast appears, the general Chinese model is still in use.

Manga mode keeps showing "No text detected" on images that clearly have text?

This depends on your screenshot method. Here are the possible causes and solutions:

MediaProjection (Screen Recording) Mode
• Protected apps block screenshots: Some apps (system photo gallery, private albums, banking, payment) use FLAG_SECURE or DRM to block MediaProjection capture. The system returns a blank screenshot, so OCR finds no text.
• Private albums: Many devices (Huawei/Honor/Xiaomi) have built-in privacy protection in their gallery apps that blocks screen capture even with MediaProjection enabled.
• Solution: Save the image to a regular folder (e.g. Downloads) and open it with a third-party image viewer, or view the content in a browser.

Accessibility Service Mode
• Same restrictions: Accessibility screenshots face the same security limitations in protected apps and private albums.
• Not inside the target app: If you're on the home screen or notification shade, the accessibility service may capture a blank area. Open the target app first, then trigger translation.
• Solution: Same as above — use a third-party viewer. Also try toggling Accessibility Service off and on in system settings.

Other Common Causes
• No recognizable text: The page may contain images, decorative text, or artistic fonts that OCR cannot recognize.
• Crop area misses text: Check that the selected area includes text. Try widening the crop.
• OCR engine mismatch: Try switching OCR engines (PP-OCRv5 ↔ ML Kit ↔ manga-ocr) in the manga floating menu — different engines handle different fonts better.
• Image quality: Blurry, low-resolution, or heavily compressed text is harder to recognize.

If nothing helps, try switching screenshot methods in Settings → About → Screenshot Method. Different devices and scenarios may have different compatibility.
Auto-translate stuck: pages don\'t change, manual translate always shows the same cached result?

This is caused by a screen capture conflict between the app's MediaProjection and the system or another app.

Symptoms:
• Auto-translate: page changes are never detected, the progress bar stays on "detecting", or a 30-second timeout dialog appears
• Manual translate: every tap shows "⚡ Cache" (cache hit) with the same translation result — new pages show the same content

Cause:
System screen recording, screen mirroring/casting, or another app's recording feature is holding the MediaProjection channel exclusively, preventing this app's VirtualDisplay from capturing new frames. Every screenshot returns the last frame before the conflict started, so pHash never changes and translation results stay frozen.

Solutions:
• Stop system screen recording: Pull down the notification shade and turn off the built-in screen recorder
• Disconnect casting: Turn off screen mirroring or casting to external displays
• Check other recording apps: Close game boosters, live streaming assistants, or other apps that might be using the recording channel
• Restart the translation service: After stopping all recording, restart manga translation from the app
• Switch to Accessibility screenshot: In Settings → About → Screenshot Method, switch to Accessibility Service — it is not affected by MediaProjection conflicts

This is a platform-level limitation affecting all apps using MediaProjection, not a bug specific to this app.
How to connect to a translation model deployed on my LAN / PC?

The app can connect to a local model service deployed on a PC in the same LAN (e.g. llama.cpp, LM Studio, Ollama) through an OpenAI-compatible API — no public API key required.

Step 1: Start the local model service on your PC
Load a model and start the service with whatever tool you use, and note the port. The key is to make the service listen on 0.0.0.0 (allow LAN access), otherwise the phone can't reach it. How to enable it per tool:
• llama-server: --host 0.0.0.0
• LM Studio: enable the LAN / remote access option in settings
• Ollama: listens on 0.0.0.0 by default, nothing to do
• Others: check the docs for an "allow remote / LAN access" option

Step 2: Find your PC LAN IP
Run ipconfig and note the IPv4 address (e.g. 192.168.1.100).

Step 3: Verify connectivity from the phone
Open http://PC-IP:port in the phone browser — if it opens, the network is OK. If it doesn't, check in order:
1. Are the phone and PC on the same LAN?
2. Is the service listening on 0.0.0.0?
3. Is the PC firewall allowing the port? (Only if it still can't connect)

Step 4: Configure in the app
Settings → API Config → Add Custom API: fill Base URL as http://PC-IP:port/v1, API Key and Model name any value, then run the connection test.

Other notes
• PC proxy does not affect phone connections (LAN is direct, no proxy)
• For plain http addresses, make sure the app version allows cleartext traffic

Uni AI Translation API Function Description

⚠️ Note: This is an advanced feature that requires you to have basic API call knowledge.

1. Basic Description
This feature allows you to use mainstream AI services for translation (as long as they are compatible with OpenAI API specifications), such as ChatGPT, Qwen, DeepSeek, etc. The integration method is through calling official API interfaces.

2. Parameter Description
1. API_KEY: The API key provided by the official website
2. Base URL: The access endpoint provided by the official website 
3. Model: The name of the model to be used
4. System Prompt: Sets the identity for the model, keep default is recommended
5. User Prompt: Translation instructions sent to the model, keep default is recommended

3. Configuration Example
Taking the integration of Alibaba's "Qwen-Plus" model as an example:
For API_KEY, fill in normally;
For Base URL, Alibaba's Qwen models generally use https://dashscope.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1;
For Model, the "Qwen-Plus" model corresponds to the code name qwen-plus;
For System Prompt and User Prompt, keep the defaults.

4. Before Using This Feature
You can first test the API response using tools like Postman, Reqable, etc. After successful testing, fill in the relevant parameters into this feature.
Not working? Try adding \"/v1\" to the end of the base URL; and \"/chat/completions\" will be added automatically.
When enabled, /chat/completions is automatically appended to the base URL. Disable if your URL already includes the full endpoint.
